hints.title: Retention Ratio Calculation
hints.text: Determine the proportion of total unique participants who logged back into the platform exactly one day following their initial session.

hints.title: First Date Self Join
hints.text: Find each user initial timestamp using a CTE or subquery, then inner join with the main table matching date plus one day.

hints.title: Retention Blueprint
hints.text: Join first login table with activity on player_id and event_date equals first_date + 1 day. Return round(count(distinct a.player_id) / total, 2).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH FirstLogin AS (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_date
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT
    ROUND(
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.player_id) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) FROM Activity),
        2
    ) AS fraction
FROM FirstLogin f
JOIN Activity a
  ON f.player_id = a.player_id
 AND a.event_date = DATE_ADD(f.first_date, INTERVAL 1 DAY);
```

variables: N: number of records in Activity table
complexity.notes: Subquery aggregation and self-join execute in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking consecutive days without verifying that the base date was the initial login overcounts later consecutive sessions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Materializing earliest login isolates baseline cohorts accurately.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of CTE or subquery with DATE_ADD and correct rounding to two decimals.

WITH FirstLogin AS (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_date
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT
    ROUND(
        COUNT(DISTINCT a.player_id)::numeric / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) FROM Activity), 0),
        2
    ) AS fraction
FROM FirstLogin f
JOIN Activity a
  ON f.player_id = a.player_id
 AND a.event_date = f.first_date + INTERVAL '1 day';

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def gameplay_analysis(activity: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    first_logins = activity.groupby('player_id')['event_date'].min().reset_index()
    first_logins['next_date'] = first_logins['event_date'] + pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    merged = pd.merge(first_logins, activity, left_on=['player_id', 'next_date'], right_on=['player_id', 'event_date'])
    total_players = activity['player_id'].nunique()
    retained_players = merged['player_id'].nunique()
    fraction = round(retained_players / total_players, 2) if total_players > 0 else 0.0
    return pd.DataFrame({'fraction': [fraction]})
